subject: genetics
question: **Type:** application You cross two true-breeding white-flowered mutants of a plant whose wild-type flowers are purple, and all F1 plants have purple flowers. What does this result indicate about the two mutations?

options.text: The mutations are in the same gene, so the F1 is expected to be white.
The mutations are dominant alleles of the same gene.
The mutations are in different genes, and each parent supplies a functional allele the other lacks.
The F1 shows incomplete dominance at a single gene.

explanation: **Complementation** occurs when two recessive mutations lie in different genes: the F1 receives a functional copy of gene 1 from one parent and a functional copy of gene 2 from the other, restoring purple. If both mutations were in the same gene, no F1 plant would have a functional allele and the F1 would be white, contradicting A and B. Incomplete dominance would give an intermediate color at a single locus, not full purple.
